subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should persisted `/exec` session exec fields continue to override later agent/global `tools.exec` config, or should operator config changes reset or dominate those stored session defaults?
rationale: Current source, tests, and docs intentionally treat `/exec` as durable session state, but the issue identifies a real security-policy enforcement gap when operators later tighten global config.

options.title: Add resettable session defaults
options.body: Keep `/exec` as per-session behavior but add an explicit migration, doctor repair, or reset/config-generation boundary so operator security changes can clear or dominate stale stored exec fields.

options.title: Make global config dominant
options.body: Change resolver precedence so global or agent config wins over stored session fields, accepting a documented behavior break for existing session defaults.

options.title: Keep current contract
options.body: Leave persisted session overrides as-is and clarify operator guidance that hard-disable requires tool policy or session reset.

recommendation.title: Add resettable session defaults
recommendation.body: Keep `/exec` as per-session behavior but add an explicit migration, doctor repair, or reset/config-generation boundary so operator security changes can clear or dominate stale stored exec fields.

likelyOwner.reason: The history points to this owner for the original `/exec` session override behavior and the current resolver/docs coverage.
